item.title: Iran War: Trump or Iran Just Overplayed Their Hand
item.description: A chance was missed last week to put the standoff between the US and Iran on a path toward settlement rather than escalation: Tehran made an offer and Donald Trump refused it. The attempt failed because neither was ready to compromise, and if that’s the end of the matter one side will have overplayed its hand. The question is which — and that does not have a simple answer.
item.dc:creator: Marc Champion

item.title: Drumcree: Northern Ireland Peace Is Under Threat Again
item.description: The last time I was in Drumcree, the Northern Ireland tinderbox where Catholic residents are engaged in a standoff with Orange Order marchers, I was hit on the leg by a golf ball. It was launched at me by rioters as the police blocked unionists from parading down the Garvaghy Road, a pro-Irish nationalist enclave of largely Protestant Portadown.
item.dc:creator: Rosa Prince

item.title: What’s Going to Break in the Bondpocalypse?
item.description: A negative surprise in upcoming US data might be the only thing to arrest bonds’ slide.
item.dc:creator: John Authers

item.title: The 2026 NFL Season Is Off to an Ironic Start
item.description: Sports have grown more complicated with the advent of fantasy football and gambling.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Karl

item.title: A Tropical Island Drought May Make Sneakers Pricier
item.description: What could 2026 do to make the fossil fuel supply crisis emanating from the Persian Gulf just a little bit worse? How about a whole separate fossil fuel supply crisis on the other side of the world? That’s what the bone-dry weather brought by the current super-El Nino is incubating.
item.dc:creator: David Fickling

item.title: Banks Recycle the Risk
item.description: Also Nvidia’s buyback, Automattic intrigue and agentic sports betting.
item.dc:creator: Matt Levine

item.title: South Korea’s Central Bank Is Smart Not to Kill This Boom
item.description: South Korea’s remarkable economic boom can run for a while yet, if the central bank has any say in the matter. Officials do have their work cut out managing the spillovers, but restraint may prove to be the most courageous course of action.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Moss

item.title: Choosin’ Texas’ Chart Dominance Is a Wake Up Call for Music Fans
item.description: Music fans and journalists who spent the last few months looking for the song of the summer faced a plot twist fit for Hollywood: The winner was a single released last October. Billboard announced last week that Ella Langley’s Choosin’ Texas had secured the No. 1 spot on the Hot 100 chart for the 23rd week, breaking the record held by Mariah Carey’s All I Want for Christmas Is You.
item.dc:creator: Peter A. Berry

item.title: US Healthcare Crisis: Universal Public Health Insurance Is the Answer
item.description: Employer-sponsored health insurance is rapidly deteriorating. In 2027, premiums are expected to see their largest single-year increase in two decades, jumping 11% and closing in on a nearly four-fold increase this century. The amount workers pay for their portion today would have covered the entire premium in 2000.
item.dc:creator: Kathryn Anne Edwards

item.title: Election Polls: Democrats Have Room to Grow With Trump Skeptics
item.description: The most important measure to watch in the campaign’s final weeks is how Democratic candidates are performing among voters who disapprove of President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Ronald Brownstein

item.title: Congress Ought to Fix Flawed US-Saudi Nuclear Deal
item.description: The confusion surrounding a proposed civil nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia hasn’t exactly disappeared: The White House is still claiming it depends on the country normalizing relations with Israel, even if that’s not part of the written agreement. At least Congress now has the text for review. Having seen its flaws, legislators should demand changes.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Entrepreneurs Are Being Rewarded for Predatory Capitalism
item.description: A recent New York Times investigation found that sports betting company DraftKings Inc. built a machine-learning model that scored customers by how much they would lose for each free bet or bonus they received. The data analyst assigned to test the model began to worry that many of the customers ranked highest were prone to addiction. By financial logic, the analyst said, “the best investment would be a problem gambler.”
item.dc:creator: Gautam Mukunda

item.title: Driverless Trucks Show How to Keep AI Robots From Killing Us
item.description: The most bothersome aspect of the warning that artificial intelligence could wipe out humanity is that there are few details about how a rogue computer model could actually accomplish it.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Black

item.title: Warsh's Credibility Boost in Bonds Is Bessent’s Comeuppance
item.description: The stunning rise in US borrowing costs has been attributed to a panoply of factors, both bad and good, including warm inflation, persistently large budget deficits and even strong economic growth, which may be boosting demand for capital. But the latest leg up in Treasury yields looks more like a credibility windfall for Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh.
